clue.text: Hypocrisy of long line of young folk with careers

parts.note: a line of schoolchildren walking two by two is called by the name of a big reptile
to career is to rush headlong, as is to tear

explanation.surface: Young people setting out on careers are accused of hypocrisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Careers' looks like jobs but is a verb meaning rushes. A crocodile is a British term for a double file of schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names false weeping, insincere shows of sorrow, which is a form of pretended feeling and so hypocrisy.

clue.text: Company payments about to acknowledge journalists

parts.note: standard abbreviation for company

indicators.note: about means round or surrounding, so the payments word goes around the next word

parts.note: regular payments for property
to acknowledge a letter is to reply to it

explanation.surface: A firm's payments are meant to recognise the work of its reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The payments word wraps the acknowledging verb after its first letter, and the company abbreviation goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondents are reporters who send news stories, often from abroad, to a newspaper or broadcaster.

clue.text: It's eccentric to hide silver — and a gross offence

indicators.note: to hide something is to keep it covered inside, so the metal sits within the eccentric word

parts.note: outré is a French borrowing for bizarre or unconventional
chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Someone oddly hides the silver, which is a serious crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Outré is a French borrowing used in English for bizarre; 'It's' just makes the surface read as a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrage is a shocking, wicked act, a grave affront or crime against decency.

clue.text: Demosthenes, perhaps — one very big in musical compositions

parts.note: Demosthenes was a famous public speaker of ancient Athens
Roman numeral one
outsize, a clothing size label

explanation.surface: A great Greek speaker is said to be a giant figure in the music world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Demosthenes as just one example of the type. OS (outsize) is a British clothing-size label for very large garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Oratorios are large-scale sacred works for choir, soloists and orchestra, performed without staging or costume.

clue.text: Lack of activity gets tie spoiled with rain

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined and messed up, so the letters of the words that follow lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rained-on necktie leaves someone too gloomy to do anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is sluggishness, a tendency to stay still and do nothing rather than move or act.

clue.text: Welcome me turning up with support

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means flipping so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
a brace is a prop or support

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be greeted warmly when they arrive with backing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'turning up' reads the word from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or person is to accept them gladly, to greet with open arms.

clue.text: Refugee in English team meeting the French

parts.note: standard abbreviation
a cricket or football eleven, written in Roman numerals
French masculine definite article

explanation.surface: An asylum seeker plays for an English side in a match against France.
explanation.walkthrough: XI (eleven) stands for a team because cricket and football sides have eleven players.
explanation.definitionFit: An exile is a person banished from their homeland, much like someone who has fled to safety elsewhere.

clue.text: Cover up in bank, as the Queen does

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the second, which wraps around it

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upward

parts.note: to lag pipes is to wrap them in insulation

explanation.surface: A monarch is pictured hushing something up at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' must be read as a verb, as in bank on. The insulating word goes upward in this down entry and sits inside the trusting verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Regally means in a royal manner, the way a reigning sovereign behaves, so the phrase defines the adverb.

clue.text: Chandler's crate repaired by much older lover

indicators.note: repaired suggests something taken apart and put together again in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, including the s

explanation.surface: A ship's chandler gets a broken box fixed by an elderly sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: A chandler is a dealer in supplies, especially for ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A cradle-snatcher is someone who takes a partner far younger than themselves, an informal jibe.

clue.text: Artist's touch shown in fierce competition

parts.note: Royal Academician; the 's means has, joining it to the next piece
a touch of something is a slight trace

explanation.surface: A painter's deft touch is on display in a tough contest.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a member of the Royal Academy, is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the relentless struggle for success at work, a ruthless scramble to get ahead.

clue.text: Bachelor's lookalike found in carrier

parts.note: abbreviation for bachelor, as in degree titles; the 's means has
a dead ringer is an exact double

explanation.surface: A single man's double turns up in a delivery firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A bringer is one who fetches or delivers something, so it works as another word for a carrier.

clue.text: "Return of Duckweed", written by a muse

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters are read from right to left

parts.note: split as duck, a zero score in cricket shaped like a round letter, plus weed, the tares of the Bible parable

explanation.surface: A sequel called 'Return of Duckweed' is penned by an inspired poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The title splits into Duck and weed; read the joined pieces right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses of Greek myth, the one presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Time taken by one who composed, conducted and toured

parts.note: abbreviation for time
Maurice Ravel, French composer of Boléro
to conduct people is to lead them

explanation.surface: A composer-conductor takes time off and goes on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conducted' hints at an orchestra but means guided.
explanation.definitionFit: To have toured is to have journeyed from place to place, which is what travelled means.

clue.text: State spread in which apple drink is knocked back

indicators.note: in which tells us the spread holds the other piece within it

parts.note: pâté is a savoury paste spread on toast

indicators.note: knocked back, besides drunk quickly, can mean sent backwards, so the drink is read in reverse

parts.note: cider is fermented apple juice

explanation.surface: A buffet where cider is downed in one gulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking, but it means the drink is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To predicate is to assert or affirm something as true, so it can stand for the verb state.

clue.text: Convert her with my short poem!

indicators.note: to convert is to change something into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea to win a woman over with a little verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhyme can mean a brief piece of verse, such as a nursery jingle, not just matching sounds.

clue.text: Collapse of holiday — no one turned up!

parts.note: a break, as when parliament or school stops sitting

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means flipped to read bottom to top rather than arrived

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A holiday falls through because nobody showed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' looks like arriving, but in this down entry it means the last two pieces are read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A recession is an economic slump, a downturn or collapse in trade and output.

clue.text: Welsh girl involved in nunnery supervision

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within, so the name lies tucked inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A young Welsh woman takes on oversight at a convent.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerys is a girl's first name of Welsh origin, so a Welsh girl is a fair example-style definition.

clue.text: Descartes seen outside clinic, half-shattered, needing rest

indicators.note: outside means the name stands around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: first name of René Descartes, the French philosopher

indicators.note: half shattered means half destroyed, so only half of the word survives

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A philosopher, worn out, is spotted near a clinic and needs a lie-down.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep only the first half of the medical word, then place it inside the philosopher's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lie back and relax, which is a way to rest.

clue.text: Confess, yet appear decent

parts.note: to come is to arrive or show up
clean means wholesome and decent, as in clean fun

explanation.surface: Someone owns up and still seems respectable.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is an idiom for admitting the truth about something one has hidden.

clue.text: Life force in opposition to wine

parts.note: in Chinese thought, the vital energy in all things
against

explanation.surface: A vital spirit stands against drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red table wine from the Tuscany region of Italy.

clue.text: Mother has somehow eaten a sea cow

parts.note: informal word for mother

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unspecified route, so their order is free

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mum has somehow consumed an entire marine mammal.
explanation.definitionFit: The manatee is a large plant-eating aquatic mammal, commonly nicknamed the sea cow.

clue.text: Were boy to change, this might go up in disbelief

definitions.text: this might go up in disbelief

indicators.note: if the words were to change, their letters would be reshuffled into a new word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boy turning into something else would make anyone's face register astonishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description: a raised one signals doubt or surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: People lift the hair above the eye when sceptical or surprised, so it rises in disbelief.

clue.text: Drive sorted out six with no cure

indicators.note: sorted out means put into a new order, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A determined push resolves six ailments that had no remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like motivation, but here it is the noun for a trip by car.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive can be a pleasure outing in a car, which is a short trip or jaunt.

clue.text: Cheerio, Jack! Wine's included!

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white wine from the Rioja region of northern Spain.

clue.text: Author lying in the street, exhausted

indicators.note: lying in places the writer stretched out inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: abbreviation for street
a pen writes, so it stands for whoever writes

explanation.surface: A writer lies collapsed in the road, worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spent has used up all their energy and so is tired out completely.

clue.text: Hat to wear for short journey to part of Cornwall

indicators.note: short means cut off before its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: One of three rulers produces inordinately rich art
